chain.g: pertaining to a city or citizens

ety.text: Borrowed from Latin cīvicus (“pertaining to a city or citizens”).

senses.d: Of, relating to, or belonging to a city, a citizen, or citizenship; municipal or civil.
ex: Thousands of people came to the Civic Center to show off their civic pride.

senses.d: Of or relating to the citizen, or of good citizenship and its rights and duties.

grp.label: Of or relating to the citizen
Having to do with a city or the people who live there

From Middle English cyvyl, civil, borrowed from Old French civil, from Latin cīvīlis (“relating to a citizen”), from cīvis (“citizen”) ultimately from proto-Indo-European *ḱey-. Cognate with Old English hīwen (“household”), hīrǣden (“family”). More at hind; hird. (polite): Compare typologically urbane (<< Latin urbs), courteous (akin to court).

senses.d: Having to do with people and government office as opposed to the military or religion.
ex: She went into civil service because she wanted to help the people.

senses.d: Behaving in a reasonable or polite manner; avoiding displays of hostility.
ex: It was very civil of him to stop the argument.
They despise each other, but they are always civil in public.

senses.d: In a peaceful and well-ordered state.
Relating to private relations among citizens, as opposed to criminal matters.
Secular.

pt:civil.gl: civil; civilian (not relating to the military or clergy)

ety.text: Borrowed from Latin cīvīlis (“civil”), from cīvis (“citizen”). Doublet of cível.
Past participle of civilizar.
From Middle English cyvylien, from Old French civilien. Equivalent to civil + -ian.

senses.d: A person following the pursuits of civil life, especially one who is not an active member of the armed forces.
ex: An army never can be commanded or controlled by civilians.
Three civilians were apprehended by the soldiers and taken away in a military vehicle.

senses.d: A person who does not belong to a particular group or engage in a particular activity, an outsider.
ex: The bathroom was for employees only, so civilians weren't allowed to use it.
I have this vision one day that I'll walk amongst you a regular civilian.

senses.d: One skilled in civil law.
ex: Ancient civilians and writers upon government.

senses.d: A student of civil law at a university or college.
A person not affiliated with a gang.
An employee of the civil service.
Not related to the military, police or other governmental professions.
ex: The three detainees were actually army defectors wearing civilian clothing.
He worked as a civilian journalist for ten years before being employed by the public broadcaster.

grp.label: not related to the military armed forces

senses.d: An organized culture encompassing many communities, often on the scale of a nation or a people; a stage or system of social, political, or technical development.
Human society, particularly civil society.
ex: A hermit doesn't much care for civilization.
I'm glad to be back in civilization after a day with that rowdy family.

senses.d: The act or process of civilizing or becoming civilized.
ex: The teacher's civilization of the child was no easy task.

senses.d: The state or quality of being civilized.
ex: He was a man of great civilization.

senses.d: The act of rendering a criminal process civil.
